meta.title: Primordial Paradox music recipes, Nintendo first-party NES family (Kondo and Tanaka paths)
meta.citation_note: Every recipe cites source ids from knowledge/music-styles/nintendo.md section 13. Full titles, URLs and read dates live there, not here, because this directory is scanned by the project's clean-room gate.
meta.chip: NES 2A03 only (2 pulse, triangle, noise, DPCM); no first-party game in this scope used an expansion chip
meta.reference_rule: study only; no melody transcribed, ripped, traced or decompiled

measured_anchors.note: all from D:/Musikage-Corpus/style-pp/stats/nintendo.json, cited as N20 in the study; its tempo field is normalised and is not used

recipes.name: One bar rhythm cell, four statements, one change
recipes.when_to_use: The skeleton of every bright cue in this style; write it before any pitch.
forbidden: changing two parameters at once on statement four
a cell with more than four attacks (it stops being a cell)
statement four unchanged, which the melody guard and the ear both read as a loop fault

recipes.name: Neighbour wobble hook
recipes.when_to_use: The pitch content of a hook; it is the measured micro-shape of this scope.

params.one_leap_allowed: perfect fourth or fifth, at a fixed position in every repetition

forbidden: wandering beyond an octave and a half
two or more leaps inside one bar
a chromatic note inside the hook itself

recipes.name: Two bar question and answer, answer unresolved
recipes.when_to_use: Second half of every 4 or 8 bar loop.

params.answer_register: same as the question, not an octave up

forbidden: closing the answer on the tonic, which flattens the loop
answering with the identical rhythm and identical pitches (that is a repeat, not an answer)

recipes.name: Written swing, long-short pair plus one frame late
recipes.when_to_use: Bright 4/4 cues that need lilt without compound metre.

params.accent: on the first note of the pair only

forbidden: triplet timing written as a frame offset
mixing this with 12/8 grouping in the same cue
swing on a sixteenth-note drum fill

recipes.name: Compound 12/8 groove
recipes.when_to_use: Zelda and Metroid path, and any cue that should feel old or folk rather than modern.

params.bass_placement: one pitch per dotted quarter, moving by step or by chord root

forbidden: backbeat on 2 and 4 (there is no 2 and 4 in this grouping)
sixteenth runs across the group boundary without an accent
tempo above 160, where the grouping stops being audible on the noise channel

recipes.name: Walking triangle bass, eighths, two pitches
recipes.when_to_use: Under any bright hook; it is the interlock the crowd-sourced Zelda tab scores at 94 for chord-bass melody.

pitch_sources: root of the next chord as an anticipation
params.accent: impossible, triangle has no volume control, so use pitch

forbidden: a steady root pedal for more than two bars in a bright cue
bass above MIDI 52, where it collides with the inner voice at 61.8
swing or dotted rhythms in the bass line

recipes.name: Bass octave answer on bar four
recipes.when_to_use: Last bar of a four bar group, to mark the seam without a drum fill.
forbidden: doing it on every bar (it becomes the bass line)
octave drop below MIDI 36, which disappears on small speakers

recipes.name: Bass carries the hook for two bars
recipes.when_to_use: Section B, or the second pass of a loop, when the melody has been continuous for four bars.

params.melody: rests, or holds a single note
params.bass_role: plays the cell rhythm on the triangle
params.inner_voice: doubles the bass a sixth above, or drops out
params.return: melody re-enters on the fifth of the key, not the tonic

forbidden: leaving all three voices empty in those two bars
putting the drum fill in the same two bars (one change at a time)

recipes.name: Hocket, melody rests and bass answers
recipes.when_to_use: Loop seams and one bar links; the cheapest way to make five channels sound like six.

params.overlap: none, one voice sounds at a time

forbidden: more than two voices trading (it becomes a messy canon)
hocket over a busy drum pattern

recipes.name: C major bright hook default
recipes.when_to_use: Overworld and menu cues; C is 38 of the 132 measured pieces.

params.harmony: I, IV, V, vi with one borrowed chord per four bars
params.avoid_degree: 4 in the hook (it pulls to 3 and weakens the lift)

forbidden: minor-key hook in a cue meant to be cheerful
more than one borrowed chord per four bars

recipes.name: Mixolydian flat seven colour
recipes.when_to_use: Wandering overworld, travel and field cues; the measured Zelda overworld tab is Bb Mixolydian.

params.chords: I, bVII, IV, v (minor five) as an option
params.melody_use: flat seven as a passing note between 1 and 6
params.frequency: at least once per two bars

forbidden: a raised leading tone in the same phrase as the flat seven
resolving the flat seven upward to the tonic as if it were the leading tone

recipes.name: Natural minor with flat six
recipes.when_to_use: Serious, sacred or title cues; the measured Zelda main theme tab is Bb minor with VI most used.

params.progression: i, VI, III, VII or i, VI, iv, V

forbidden: harmonic minor raised seventh in the same cue, unless a boss cue takes over
diminished seventh chords, which this scope uses 63 times against 1659 major chords

recipes.name: Neapolitan flat two stab
recipes.when_to_use: Danger, boss entry, secret rooms; measured at 41 occurrences of the bII6/5 bigram.

params.chord: major triad a semitone above the tonic
params.duration: one beat, then resolve to V or i6/4
params.register: below the melody, above MIDI 48 for the root

forbidden: flat two in a bright overworld loop
flat two twice in a row

recipes.name: Tonic second-inversion pedal
recipes.when_to_use: Long loops that would otherwise sit still; I6/4 is the fourth most common label in the measured corpus.

params.upper_voices: move over the pedal, or arpeggiate the tonic triad

forbidden: pedal held for more than four bars without an upper-voice change
pedal under a melody that also sits on the fifth (the two blur)

recipes.name: Suspended dominant, held then resolved
recipes.when_to_use: Loop end and phrase end; Vsus4 is the third most common single chord label (329 beats).

params.chord: V with a fourth instead of a third
params.resolution: third of the dominant, then I or i
params.where: last two beats of the loop
params.voicing: arpeggio at frame rate if only one pulse is free

forbidden: resolving sus4 to sus4 again at the loop seam
sus4 in the same bar as a diminished chord

recipes.name: Chromatic approach bass
recipes.when_to_use: Transitions between sections, and under any chord change that would otherwise be a plain root jump.

params.approach: one semitone below the next root, on the last eighth of the bar
params.range: within the 40 to 52 MIDI bass window
params.melody_state: avoid the same pitch class in the melody at that moment

forbidden: chromatic approach on every chord change
approach in the hook bar of a bright cue

recipes.name: Inner voice arpeggio at frame rate
recipes.when_to_use: Atmosphere cues; the corpus has an inner voice in every piece (204 against 132 melodies).

params.rate: one note per frame, about 60 per second
params.role: fills harmony the lead is not playing

forbidden: arpeggio in the same register as the lead
arpeggio pattern that changes per bar, which turns a texture into a tune

recipes.name: Echo pulse one sixteenth late
recipes.when_to_use: Titles, caves, underground cues; the classic cheap space effect on two pulse channels.

params.delay: one sixteenth, or one eighth at slow tempo
params.duty: 12.5 percent where the lead is 25 or 50
params.content: the lead line, unaltered, or the last note of each phrase only

forbidden: echo louder than the lead
a second echo layer (there is no third pulse on the stock chip)
echo under a long-note ambient lead, where it just thickens the drone

recipes.name: Noise kit, straight
recipes.when_to_use: Any bright cue with a running character.

params.hat: eighths or sixteenths at volume 2 to 4
params.kick: DPCM on 1 and 3, or a short pitched noise drop if no DPCM budget
params.fill: none inside 8 bars; one two-beat fill at the loop seam

forbidden: kick, snare and hat inside one sixteenth (one noise channel)
fills in the same bar as the hook's altered statement

recipes.name: Noise kit, pulse only
recipes.when_to_use: Atmosphere and danger cues in the Tanaka path.

params.content: a single noise pulse on the tonic pulse of each bar, or a low-rate noise swell
params.density: one or two events per bar
params.volume: 5 to 8, because there is nothing else in that band

forbidden: a backbeat in a cue whose harmony is doing the tension
noise on every beat, which reads as a machine rather than as unease

recipes.name: Long-note ambient lead
recipes.when_to_use: Metroid path; the measured Brinstar tab records 4 or more beats per melody note.

params.vibrato: from 120 ms into notes of 2 beats or longer
params.inner_voice: arpeggio or drone, never a countermelody

forbidden: sixteenth runs in the lead
a drum backbeat under it
a melody that moves more than an octave and a half across the cue

recipes.name: Melody on chord tones under dense harmony
recipes.when_to_use: Atmosphere cues where the harmony carries the interest (Brinstar tension 8 with chord complexity 95).

params.chromaticism: in the inner voices and the bass only
params.novelty_target: high (the tab scores 95), so borrow chords freely underneath

forbidden: chromatic notes in the lead in the same bar as a borrowed chord
two borrowed chords in adjacent bars in a non-boss cue

recipes.name: Melody against simple harmony, high tension
recipes.when_to_use: Kondo path: the Mario overworld tab scores tension 96 over chord complexity 45.

params.harmony: I, IV, V, vi only, one chord per two beats
params.melody: leans on ninths, fourths and suspensions over the chord
params.rhythm: sixteenth surface, 80 percent or more single sixteenths

forbidden: dense harmony underneath (it turns tension into mud)
more than four chords in the loop

recipes.name: Hurry-up variant
recipes.when_to_use: Time limit in any stage cue; the SMB archive holds separate Hurry entries for six cues.

params.length: same bars as the parent cue

forbidden: changing the melody (the listener must recognise it instantly)
dropping the bass (the cue loses its pulse at higher tempo)

recipes.name: Theme reuse as variation
recipes.when_to_use: Across one game: title, overworld, underground, boss.
forbidden: a variation that keeps the cell, the key, the register and the drums (that is the same cue)
more than three variations, which spends the identity

recipes.name: Title jingle under four bars, half cadence
recipes.when_to_use: Title screens and menus, before the loop proper.

params.tail: one bar of echo, then silence

forbidden: a full authentic cadence (the jingle should hand over to the loop, not close)
sixteenth-note runs longer than one beat

recipes.name: Stage clear fanfare, two bars, V to I
recipes.when_to_use: Stage clear, level complete, and any short reward cue.

params.voices: lead plus triangle, drums on the last beat only if any
params.progression: V (or Vsus4) to I, or a rising tonic arpeggio
params.rhythm: even eighths or a dotted figure, no sixteenth runs

forbidden: looping (this is a one shot)
a half cadence, which reads as unfinished
more than two bars, which is the whole Punch-Out cue budget

recipes.name: Optional expansion arrangement
recipes.when_to_use: Only if a cue is being arranged outside the game, for example a title theme rendered on a VRC6-capable engine.

params.use: pad and string doubling, melody unchanged
params.scope_note: no first-party NES game in this scope shipped with an expansion chip

forbidden: three new melodies on the new channels
claiming an expansion arrangement as authentic to this scope

recipes.name: Miss and death cue, descending, no drums
recipes.when_to_use: Player death, miss, game over.

params.motion: descending by step, or the last four notes of the scale
params.ending: dominant or a bare fifth, not the tonic

forbidden: drums (the silence is the joke)
the same contour as the stage clear fanfare

recipes.name: Eight bar loop with a one bar link
recipes.when_to_use: The default form for any stage cue in this style.

params.structure: 4 bar statement, 4 bar answer, with bar 4 and bar 8 as links
params.link_content: bass octave answer, drum fill, or a single held note
params.variation: one element changed on the second pass

forbidden: a link longer than one bar (the link becomes the theme)
changing the link every pass (it stops being a seam)

recipes.name: One frame push on the peak note
recipes.when_to_use: The highest note of the hook, once per cue, as the human touch.

params.companion: vibrato on the same note if it lasts two beats

forbidden: pushing several notes (it reads as sloppy timing)
pushing the note before a drum fill (the two smears together)

recipes.name: Sound effects tuned to the cue's key
recipes.when_to_use: Any cue in a stage where the player triggers effects often (jump, coin, block).

params.coin: tonic or fifth of the current key, one short pulse blip
params.jump: sweep that ends on the fifth or the tonic
params.rule: the effect table takes the cue's tonic as a parameter, never a fixed pitch
params.reason: effects and music share the pulse channels, so effect pitch is heard as harmony

forbidden: a fixed-pitch coin across cues in different keys
an effect that lands on the third of the key during a sus4 chord
